---
title: "Reporting, allocation and classification"
subtitle: "3.13 · constructed examples after the postrank theory book, ch. 17 and 19"
description: "Pairwise reporting, allocation and classification can lead to different decisions under the same posterior."
---

The unit with the highest posterior mean can differ from the unit most likely to rank first. A grade report
states directions between units. Allocating a place from that report requires a rule for choosing among
units in the same grade. Classification at a threshold requires costs for false positives and false negatives.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Three units, reporting objective.** The report has risk .1833. Filling a place from its highest grade selects
  a unit with expected value 4.000 and top-set overlap .700. The figure gives each quantity its own scale.
- **Three units, mean-value order.** Selecting A instead gives value 6.000 but top-set overlap .300; the strict
  report's risk is .4667. The top-set order in the table prefers B. Choosing a first recipient does not require
  publishing every comparison in a strict order.
- **Two units, τ .25.** The reporting optimum withholds. The added allocation lottery still fills a place,
  giving expected value 5.000 and overlap .500. It draws the required number of units from the boundary grade.
- **False-negative cost 3.** The threshold rule declares 2 positive, with cost .700. The convention
  “positive through the highest grade” declares only B positive and costs .900. Neither τ nor the place budget
  sets the probability cutoff for this decision. Under **Threshold 4**, being exactly at the substantive threshold does not count as above it. The threshold rule declares 0 positive, at cost .300. The grade cutoff permits both none-positive and all-positive decisions: those actions remain
  distinct even if a canonical grade representation would lose the distinction.
- **Equal reporting risk, different classifications.** Reports 2/1/2 and 3/1/2, in A/B/C order, both have risk .2000. With the same
  added grade cutoff, they declare 3 and 2 positive, at costs 1.700 and 1.300. Equal reporting risk does not
  make the added actions equivalent.
- **League, five places.** Mean-score selection gives value .558 and estimated overlap 2.733. The top-set order
  gives estimated overlap 2.825. These membership probabilities use the displayed posterior draws; their ordering
  and overlap evaluation use the same draws.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
In these examples, value is the target value of a selected unit. We calculate outcomes exactly for the finite laws.
For the league, we calculate the normal means and threshold probabilities analytically and estimate top-set
membership and overlap from draws. The league's reporting optimum is over contiguous cuts of the posterior-mean
order under a grade cap. The strict comparison reports do not belong to that family.
:::

Standalone: [one-place](../../embed/one-place.html), for example `?mode=threshold&falseNegativeCost=3`.

Related applications: [Restrictions imposed by a fixed order](order-misses.qmd), [The decision for an isolated pair](../grades/one-pair.qmd).
